goals.title: Complete Oyatie through small, merge-safe waves. Hard constraints: us...
goals.objective: Complete Oyatie through small, merge-safe waves. Hard constraints: use isolated worktree branches from fresh origin/dev; one writer per hot file; never hand-edit *.generated.json; Rust + Buck2 are authoritative; no Cargo-based verification authority; retire shell/Python/CLI authority; cloud-ci must be universal, productized, hermetic, comprehensive, cloud-native, Kubernetes-native, and API-driven; GitHub Actions is a transitional adapter only; repo-specific behavior belongs in policy data packs, not universal engines; remove active GraphQL residue without rewriting historical/vendor truth; after each wave review, fix, verify, open PR, wait for oya-ci-required green, merge, and clean up. Prefer disjoint lanes that cannot create merge conflicts. Next focus: advance cloud-ci toward universal API-driven product boundaries without touching hot workflow files unless it is the sole lane.

goals.title: M0 trunk and active PR intake
goals.objective: Keep dev green and merge-safe: finish or retire active PR/worktree lanes, verify oya-ci-required, clean stale branches/worktrees, and maintain a current backlog view before opening new broad waves.
goals.evidence: G002-m0-trunk-and-active-pr-intake complete for intake/fanout gating: no open PRs targeting dev; origin/dev 490311b9fd9cd3e65e139073d8a40e579f8e49b2 has oya-ci-required success at 2026-06-26T22:40:05Z; current collision map is .omx/team-ledgers/g002-intake-collision-map.md; post-prune summary is .omx/team-ledgers/g002-post-prune-summary.md; 30 clean/merged worktrees removed and 32 clean branch no-PR checkouts removed with branch refs preserved; final classification .omx/context/g002-intake/final-worktree-classification-20260626T2322Z.json shows 29 intentionally preserved worktrees: leader root dirty/behind, 18 dirty investigate, 10 detached not in origin/dev. G015 must launch only from fresh origin/dev worktrees and must not use preserved dirty/detached worktrees.

goals.title: M1 repo hygiene and runtime-state boundaries
goals.objective: Remove or fence root scratch artifacts, runtime-state directory drift, piled worktrees, invalid hook output, and active GraphQL residue while preserving generated files, historical ADR truth, and local runtime state boundaries.
goals.evidence: Prior plan and handoff identify root hygiene, .claude/.codex/.omc/.omx drift, SessionStart JSON, and GraphQL residue as parallel-safe hygiene lanes.

goals.title: M2 universal cloud-ci product substrate
goals.objective: Move CI from repo-specific bridge scripts toward universal Rust cloud-ci APIs: policy data packs in, hermetic gate/result packets out, GitHub Actions as adapter only, Buck2 authoritative, no shell/Python authority.
goals.evidence: Latest user directive: cloud native, API driven; CI must be universal, productized, hermetic, comprehensive, not Oyatie-specific.

goals.title: M3 generated-artifact conflict elimination
goals.objective: Remove generated artifact merge surfaces by using Rust materializers/controllers, de-committed pure derivations, drift compare gates, and controller-owned repair PRs; never hand-edit generated JSON.
goals.evidence: User called generated slices causing merge conflict an anti-pattern and requested a more elegant solution or removal.

goals.title: M4 Rust purity and Python/MJS authority retirement
goals.objective: Align Rust latest-stable policy, Buck2 toolchain, dependency automation, shell/Python/MJS retirement, and no local CLI authority under reusable Rust apps and APIs. Replace Python and MJS only where they still provide valid, worth-preserving live authority; delete, fence, or leave historical/vendor-only scripts instead of rewriting dead code.
goals.evidence: User requested Rust 2024 latest stable everywhere, own/dependabot-like updating, shell/Python retirement, and API-based no-CLI operation.
goals.steeringEvidence: User requested starting Python and MJS replacement to Rust, clarified only if still valid and worth preserving, and invoked ponytail minimalism.
goals.steeringRationale: This is a narrower wording update to existing G006, preserving the aggregate objective while preventing speculative rewrites.

Each worker owns a non-overlapping slice, opens PRs only when justified, and reports verification/merge readiness.
goals.evidence: User explicitly requested Team for each wave and disjoint areas where each Team takes its slice end-to-end.

goals.title: M15 Hyperscaler process and closed-loop review
goals.objective: For every wave, assess parallelizable work, friction/process failures, merge-conflict risk, verification gaps, enterprise/hyperscaler readiness, security/performance posture, and plan quality; feed fixes back into the next wave before launching it.

teamExecutionPolicy.launchRule: Before each wave, run a team preflight snapshot, launch team workers only on disjoint file/path ownership, and do not advance to the next wave until all wave PRs are reviewed, fixed, green, merged, and cleaned up.
teamExecutionPolicy.conflictPolicy: One writer per hot file. Shared workflow files, oya-ci.toml, root hub specs, generated-artifact policies, and generated files are single-writer serial lanes. Friction or merge conflict is process failure.
teamExecutionPolicy.modelPolicy: Use gpt-5.5 with high reasoning for build/planning/review/team execution where runtime supports explicit launch args; do not use spark for planning/review/build work.
teamExecutionPolicy.workerCountLayout: 1|5|5 tmux windows where possible: leader + two five-worker teams for disjoint wave halves
teamExecutionPolicy.reviewPosture: Torvalds-strict critic for process/code slop; hyperscaler architect for APIs, tenancy, security, operations, scalability, and production readiness
